tagline: Three days up the Inside Passage on the state's own ferries.
intro: This road begins at a dock. From Bellingham the mainline ferries take just under three days to reach Skagway, working north through the Inside Passage, where more than 1,500 islands keep off the big Pacific surges. Cabins cost extra. Every mainline boat has a solarium and lounges for sleeping, and tent cities commonly go up at the stern.
It is a working line before it is anything else, carrying people, freight and vehicles to Southeast towns that no road reaches, and most of the food is served cafeteria-style.

moments.title: Petroglyph Beach, Wrangell
moments.text: Barely a mile out of Wrangell, at least 40 Tlingit carvings of whales, salmon and faces sit on the shore boulders, some of them below the high-tide line.

moments.title: Petersburg
moments.text: Little Norway keeps Norwegian Constitution Day for several days in May, and townspeople who visited Norway found their celebration runs longer than Norway's own.

moments.title: Skagway
moments.text: The first boatload of Klondike prospectors landed here in July 1897, and the narrow-gauge White Pass and Yukon Route still sets out from the port each summer.

practical: Service drops off considerably in winter, when the vessels usually go in for overhauls.
